title: Ivo and the Bell
premise: Mara Vane, a late-night radio host, begins receiving calls from listeners who died the previous week—voices that know his name and hum a tune from his childhood. When Ivo, the imaginary friend he invented at seven and abandoned at twelve, appears on his porch unchanged by time, Mara learns that 'imaginary' was a euphemism: Ivo is a bell-ringer for something that counts the living each frost. The dead callers are those who were counted and not claimed. To save his estranged family, Mara must break a promise he made as a child, ring the bell himself in Ivo's place, and accept that belonging means being seen—even by the thing that counts.
about_author: Marguerite Nystrom is the pen name of a former overnight radio producer who spent years convinced the dead air between calls was never quite empty. She writes horror from a farmhouse in northern Sweden, where the frost arrives early and patterns on the windows are never quite symmetrical.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Mara. During his nightly call-in show, Mara takes a call from Doris Halloway, a devoted listener—and realizes mid-conversation that her obituary ran six days ago. He tells himself it's a prank, but her voice knows things only Doris knew. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in seven years of rational explanations.

chapters.title: The Porch Light
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Arriving home at 3 a.m., Mara finds a small figure waiting on his porch: Ivo, exactly as he was thirty years ago, same patched coat, same patient smile. Ivo says only, 'You stopped answering. The count doesn't stop.' Mara locks the door and tells no one. Emotional beat: terror braided with an awful, homesick tenderness.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A second dead caller phones in—a man whose death Mara inadvertently announced on air last winter. Between calls, Ivo sits outside all night, unmoving, unbothered by frost. Mara digs out childhood drawings and finds Ivo rendered in every one, always standing slightly behind him. Emotional beat: evidence accumulating against denial.

chapters.title: What We Agreed
chapters.summary: POV Mara, with flashback chapters to age seven. Memory surfaces: lonely boy, invented friend, then the night the friend answered back—and the bargain struck so the family would be left alone. Mara broke it at twelve by pretending Ivo out loud into nothing. Emotional beat: guilt reframed; he didn't imagine Ivo away, he betrayed him.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes
chapters.summary: POV Mara's sister, Nell, visiting with her two kids after their mother's stroke. Nell notices window frost forming tally marks overnight and a small extra place setting her son insists on laying for 'the quiet man.' Mara begs her to leave town; she thinks he's unraveling. Emotional beat: isolation deepening—the cost of being believed too late.

chapters.title: Callers
chapters.summary: POV Mara. On air, the dead callers stop asking for comfort and start delivering instructions: names, dates, the phrase 'before the final pattern.' One caller is his mother's late neighbor, warning that the count reaches whole households. Mara finally speaks to Ivo through the door. Emotional beat: surrender of the last excuse—he must listen now.

chapters.title: Ivo's Side
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A single chapter from inside the bell-ringer's existence: centuries of counting, of children who invented him as shields, of the one rule—that a ringer may be replaced only by someone who loves him enough to take the rope. Ivo has waited thirty years not for revenge but for Mara to choose him freely. Emotional beat: devastating sympathy for the monster-friend.

chapters.title: The Final Pattern
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Hard frost forecast. The tally marks on Nell's windows complete themselves name by name. Mara gets his family onto the road south, but the highway loops back twice, and the radio plays only his own show, broadcasting from a studio that burned down in 1994. Emotional beat: rising dread as escape proves to be part of the design.

chapters.title: Rope and Bell
chapters.summary: POV Mara. In the bell tower beneath his childhood house—a house that was never his—Mara faces the counter-thing and takes the rope from Ivo's hands, ringing the bell in his stead and speaking his own true name into the count. The claim transfers. Ivo weeps for the first time in centuries. Emotional beat: climax—love against duty, paid in full.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: POV Mara, epilogue months later. The show continues; the dead have stopped calling, though some nights static shapes itself into a familiar hum. Nell's kids remember 'the quiet man' fondly. On the last page, Mara signs off the broadcast and, alone in the studio, answers a knock at the door—not with fear, but with the porch light already on. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging chosen, identity claimed, love outlasting the count.
